title: Deceptive Grounding: When RAG Cites the Right Text, Wrong Entity
hook: A RAG system can pass every faithfulness, hallucination, and citation check while quietly citing the wrong entity's evidence — real text, real citation, wrong subject.
key_points: Deceptive grounding: every cited claim is real and retrieved, but attributed to the wrong entity (Drug Y's evidence as Drug X's).
Invisible to standard faithfulness, hallucination, and citation checks, since the citations genuinely exist and are relevant.
Across 13 models, rates hit 8-87% under adversarial conditions; medical fine-tuning made it worse, not better (up to 86.7%).
Found in 7.8% of cases from a real, deployed production RAG system — this isn't just a lab artifact.
A simple entity-attribution consistency check (cited evidence matches queried entity) catches it at 97% precision, 98.7% recall.
content_html: Standard RAG evaluation checks whether a model's claims are grounded in retrieved documents — not whether that evidence is about the right entity. Caruzzo, Yoo, and Kim show a RAG system can pass every faithfulness, hallucination, and citation check while quietly presenting one entity's evidence as another's. They call this deceptive grounding, and it's a lesson for any multi-entity RAG system, not just clinical ones.
extra_html: Using clinical drug Q&A as the illustrating case — swap in any domain where a system fields questions about many similar, easily-confused entities and the failure mode is the same — the authors run a controlled benchmark across 13 models and find deceptive-grounding rates from 8% up to 87% under adversarial conditions. An ablation pins down the mechanism: strip entity-specific evidence from the retrieved documents and the failure shifts entirely to confabulation instead, showing both failure modes share the same root trigger. Measured on a real production system across 740 drug-disease pairs, deceptive grounding still showed up in 7.8% of cases (13.6% for recently approved drugs), confirming it isn't just a benchmark artifact. The fix the authors propose is simple: a consistency check verifying that cited evidence actually concerns the queried entity, which catches deceptive grounding at 97% precision and 98.7% recall — something no existing RAG evaluation framework currently implements. Cedric Caruzzo, Donggeun Yoo, and Tae Soo Kim, arXiv 2026 (arxiv.org/abs/2607.09349).

related.title: Why RAG? Grounding LLMs in Your Data
related.hook: An LLM only knows what it was trained on — until it's stale, private, or just wrong. RAG bolts on a search step so the model answers from your data and can cite it.

related.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
related.hook: Why force a model to memorize everything? RAG lets it look things up — fetch relevant documents, then answer from that evidence instead of frozen weights alone.

flashcards.prompt: What is 'deceptive grounding' in a RAG system?
flashcards.back_html: A failure where every cited claim is real, retrieved, and topically relevant — but attributed to the wrong entity, like presenting Drug Y's evidence as Drug X's.

flashcards.prompt: Why do standard faithfulness and citation checks miss deceptive grounding?

choices.text: Because the citations genuinely exist and are relevant text — nothing about them looks fabricated
Because faithfulness checks don't look at citations at all
Because the model refuses to cite anything in these cases

flashcards.explanation_html: Faithfulness and hallucination checks verify claims trace back to real retrieved text — they don't verify which entity that text is actually about.

flashcards.prompt: Did domain fine-tuning reduce deceptive grounding in the study?
flashcards.back_html: No — medical/biomedical fine-tuned models showed higher rates, up to 86.7%, meaning domain specialization amplified the failure rather than fixing it.

flashcards.prompt: What detects deceptive grounding effectively, per the paper?

choices.text: An entity-attribution consistency check verifying cited evidence matches the queried entity
Running the existing hallucination detector twice
Increasing the number of retrieved documents

flashcards.explanation_html: This check — does the cited evidence actually concern the entity being asked about — caught it at 97% precision and 98.7% recall.
